name: Copying the Hadamard-loop state
summary: An X-spider with a Hadamard self-loop (the state |1⟩) is copied by a Z-spider.
description:
A spider with a Hadamard self-loop is equal, up to a scalar, to the same spider with an extra π phase (see [Hadamard self-loop removal](../hadamard-self-loop-removal/)). So an X-spider with a Hadamard self-loop and one leg is the computational basis state $|1\rangle$ (up to a scalar), and like any basis state it is copied by a Z-spider.

Duncan and Perdrix used this rule, written with self-loops instead of π phases, as an axiom of their *angle-free* ZX-calculus, in which there are no phases at all: π phases are replaced by Hadamard self-loops (the H-loop axiom). They showed that this calculus is complete for real stabilizer quantum mechanics.
parameter_notes: n is the number of legs of the Z-spider (shown for n = 2).

source.location: Section 'Angle-free calculus for Real Stabilizers', axiom (L)
